property_summary: A transfer whose sender and recipient are both blacklisted always reverts, while the same transfer succeeds once either address is un-blacklisted.

While no distribute address is configured (the initial state, which cannot be changed by any external caller since the CFO is unset), distributeTokenPeriodic must always revert and must not change the contract's token balance.
setCaller rejects the zero address, and once a CFO is set by the owner, setWhite can only be invoked by that CFO, reverting for any other caller.

After the owner configures a distribute address and funds the contract, distributeTokenPeriodic transfers exactly 2000e18 tokens to it and cannot execute again until 64800 seconds have passed (reverts immediately on a second call in the same block).

After the owner configures a distribute address and funds the contract, distributeTokenPeriodic transfers exactly 2000e18 tokens to it, and a second call in the same block reverts without moving tokens.

A transfer of any amount from the whitelisted deployer (the test contract) always succeeds and moves exactly that amount, charging no fee: recipient balance increases by amount and sender balance decreases by amount.
A transfer reverts if and only if both sender and recipient are blacklisted; otherwise it succeeds moving exactly the amount.
compiler_error: a state-changing call on c is not a plain top-level statement, or c is reached through a low-level call / abi.encodeWithSignature / address cast / interface / helper. Every call must be `c.f(args);`, `x = c.f(args);`, or `try c.f(args) { ... } catch { ... }` at top level of the single public function; only view calls may sit inside require/assert

property_summary: After approving a spender for amount a, transferring x (with a >= x and x <= balance) via transferFrom moves exactly x to the recipient and reduces the allowance by exactly x.
Admin functions gated by onlyCaller (e.g. setBlack) revert when the caller is not the cfo, and succeed once the owner assigns a cfo via setCaller.

distributeTokenPeriodic moves exactly 2000e18 tokens from the contract to the distribute address, and a second call in the same block reverts because distribution is allowed only once per 64800 seconds.
